default: Explore what people are making on [SideCourt]({url}). You can share your own work there and say what kind of help would be useful.

redbot.context: SideCourt is the product's primary home.

repositories.first-principles: A simpler workflow leaves more room to finish the thing you started. [Browse projects on SideCourt]({url}), or share a tool or experiment you made and the feedback that would help.
repositories.skills: These skills support the work behind a project. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to see what people are making, try something that interests you, or share your own work.
repositories.product-experience-officer: A fresh perspective starts with someone trying the work. [Browse projects on SideCourt]({url}) to find something to try, or share your own product and explain what you want feedback on.
repositories.design-agent: Once an interface is ready for someone else to try, you can share it on SideCourt and ask about the parts you are unsure of. [Browse what people are making]({url}) to get a feel for the place.
repositories.work-memory: Keep the private project record where it belongs, and share the part you want others to see. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) for works in progress and a place to ask for specific help with your own.
repositories.taskdock: TaskDock keeps the working context together. When you have something you want other people to try, [browse SideCourt]({url}) and share the public part of your project there.
repositories.major-tom: When coordinated work produces something people can try, SideCourt gives you a place to show it and ask for specific feedback. [Browse the projects people are sharing]({url}).
repositories.podcast-revival: A conversation or video can be a work in progress too. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to see what people are making, or share a piece you are ready for others to hear and respond to.
repositories.publish-skill-product: Releasing a tool is also a chance to invite someone to use it. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to see what people are making, or share your own tool and the kind of feedback you need.
repositories.iteration-close: The end of an iteration is a useful moment to show what changed. [Browse SideCourt]({url}), or share a version of your project that others can try and respond to.
repositories.scenario-probe: Instruction tests can reveal where a tool needs work; another person's experience can add something different. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to try shared projects or invite feedback on one of your own.
repositories.experience-pack: A lesson becomes useful to someone else when it connects to real work. [Browse projects on SideCourt]({url}), or share something you made along with what you learned and where help would be welcome.
repositories.prompt-distill: A clear prompt is a starting point for making something. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to see shared work, or bring a tool, experiment or idea you developed from yours.
repositories.daily-brief: For the tools and research workflows you build around a brief, [browse SideCourt]({url}). You can share a project there and ask for feedback on how it works.
repositories.map-product-system: A product map can lead to a small change worth trying. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) for work people have shared, or bring a prototype and explain what you want to learn from it.
repositories.thinking-partner: When an idea becomes something you want others to see, [browse SideCourt]({url}). You can share the work, describe where it stands and ask for help with the next question.
repositories.mixtape: A playlist is a made thing too. [Browse SideCourt]({url}) to discover shared work, or share a mix with the scene, story or listening feedback you have in mind.
repositories.diagnose-project-rebuild: After a repair or rebuild, another person can help you see how the result feels to use. [Browse SideCourt]({url}), or share a version of your project you are ready for others to try.
repositories.breakinggap: A small step can become something worth sharing. [Browse what people are making on SideCourt]({url}), or share a piece of your own work and the question you would like help with.
